reason: Route.fetch's timeout option bounds a fetch of the route's request that Strider has no call for: the request client is missing (method-route-fetch), and Route's decisions take no fetch with a deadline. Playwright's second check, that page.goto times out, has no port of its own without the first, since the route's error is what the original's assertion reads

Route.fetch's url option fetches another URL for the route to fulfill with: Strider has no Route.fetch (method-route-fetch), so the route can't send that request and answer with its response. Route.continueWith(setUrl) changes the request itself, which is a different behavior (page-request-continue's RO-062 covers it)

Route.fetch's postData option sends the route's request with a body the route gives, whatever its method (the original's is a GET navigation), and fulfills with that response: Strider has no Route.fetch (method-route-fetch). Route.continueWith of a body on a GET navigation doesn't send it on Chromium, so it can't stand in for it
